result.topic_en: Section 57 of Ramanujan's work on highly composite numbers: the generalized divisor function d_r(N), defined by the Dirichlet series of zeta(s)^{1+r}, its product formula, simple properties, and the form of N for which d_r(N) is of maximum order.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 $^{18(37)}$ (37) (73)
57. Let $d_r(N)$ denote the coefficient of $N^{-s}$ in the expansion of $\{\zeta(s)\}^{1+r}$ as a Dirichlet series. Then since
$\{\zeta(s)\}^{-1} = (1-2^{-s})(1-3^{-s})(1-5^{-s})\cdots\cdots(1-p^{-s})\cdots\cdots,$
it is easy to see that, if
$N = p_1^{a_1} p_2^{a_2} p_3^{a_3} \cdots\cdots p_n^{a_n},$
where $p_1, p_2, p_3 \cdots$ are any primes, then
(295) $d_r(N) = \prod_{\nu=1}^{\nu=n} \prod_{\lambda=1}^{\lambda=a_\nu} \left(1+\frac{r}{\lambda}\right).$
provided that $r > -1$. It is evident that
$d_{-1}(N) = 0,\ d_0(N) = 1,\ d_1(N) = d(N);$
and that, if $-1 \leq r \leq 0$, then
(296) $d_r(N) \leq 1+r$
for all values of $N$. It is also evident that, if $N$ is a prime then
$d_r(N) = 1+r$
for all values of $r$. It is easy to see from (295) that, if $r>0$, then $d_r(N)$ is not bounded when $N$ becomes infinite.
Now, if $r$ is positive, it can easily be shown that, in order that $d_r(N)$ should be of maximum order, $N$ must be of the form
$e^{\vartheta(x_1) + \vartheta(x_2) + \vartheta(x_3) + \cdots\cdots}$,
and consequently $d_r(N)$ of the form
$(1+r)^{\pi(x_1)} \left(1+\frac{r}{2}\right)^{\pi(x_2)} \left(1+\frac{r}{3}\right)^{\pi(x_3)} \cdots\cdots;$
and proceeding as in §46 we can show that $N$ must be of the form
(297) $e^{\vartheta(1+r)^x + \vartheta(1+\frac{r}{2})^x + \vartheta(1+\frac{r}{3})^x + \cdots}$
